audioDescription: Silent preview with no audio track.
limitations: Browser real-time approximation of photorealism. Nothing was photographed or path-traced.
Floor caustics are a first-order analytic estimate, 1/(1+k·∇²h), from the same height field that bends the water normals. They are not traced photon caustics, and the gain k is chosen for appearance.
The glass focus spot and dimmed footprint use an analytic ball-lens model. Metal-node light occlusion on the caustic layer is an analytic ray-sphere test, while shadows use the PCF shadow map.
Refraction uses three.js transmission render-target sampling. The glass refracts the floor but not the water surface.
The ambient water phase eases to rest by 2.6 s so the final hold is still. This is a presentation choice, not real water behaviour.
The ripple is emitted when the glass comes to rest. No wake is simulated along its rolling path.
three r186 removed PCFSoftShadowMap, so soft shadows use PCFShadowMap with shadow.radius.
The full-video route (Blender PBR, Cycles, baked simulation) is unavailable here and is reported as missing.
Typography is system Georgia / Times New Roman.
